FXUS62 KRAH 070701
AFDRAH

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
300 AM EDT Mon Sep 7 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

* Dry/continental air related to high pressure that will build 
  across and offshore the Middle Atlantic will favor lower surface 
  dewpoints/afternoon RH and low temperatures, both of which have 
  been adjusted lower by several degrees than the NBM/official 
  forecast, through Wed.
  

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 300 AM Monday...

1) Seasonable start to the second week of September

2) Above normal temperatures return by mid week, with increasing 
shower/storm chances Thursday and Friday

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 300 AM Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Seasonable start to the second week of 
September

A lower mid-latidue/subtropical ridge over the srn Plains will 
progress ewd and reach the Carolinas by 12Z Wed. Rising heights and 
weakening nwly flow aloft will result over cntl NC. 

Beneath and downstream of the ridge aloft, 1022 mb surface high 
pressure will build across and offshore the Middle Atlantic, while 
extending wwd into NC. Influence from the ridge and associated 
continental/dry air will favor mixed/afternoon surface dewpoints in 
the 50s, except lwr 60s in the Coastal Plain and ern Sandhills and 
also low temperatures in the 50s to lwr 60s. 

KEY MESSAGE 2... Above normal temperatures return by mid week, with 
increasing shower/storm chances Thursday and Friday

Strong ridging will remain in place across much of the southern US 
through mid week, with H5 heights forecast to steadily increase 
across NC through Wednesday (peaking around 594-596dm). Meanwhile at 
the surface, a 1025mb ridge off the Mid Atlantic coast will support 
increasing southerly flow area-wide. While dewpoints will be slow to 
recover and remain in the low to mid 60s on Wednesday, they will 
climb markedly Thursday into Friday with upper 60s to lower 70s 
becoming increasingly common. This will translate into steadily 
increasing heat index values reaching the mid 90s Thursday and 
Friday. 

As the upper ridge continues to flatten, we'll eventually see a 
longwave trough and attendant surface cold front move out of the 
Ohio Valley and into the Mid Atlantic/Southeast late in the week. As 
such we'll see increasing shower and storm chances as early as 
Thursday afternoon within an increasingly unstable pre-frontal 
airmass. There is still some uncertainty with respect to when the 
front/trough will move through NC (most ensemble guidance suggests 
Friday vs Thursday night), but we'll continue to maintain increased 
PoPs through the day Friday given ensemble support. That said the 
strongest forcing for ascent associated with the trough should be 
displaced well north of NC and it remains to be seen just how much 
QPF is realized with the front when it arrives. 

Precip chances should decrease in the wake of the front through the 
weekend. Temps will also decrease, albeit slightly, with highs 
reaching the upper 80s/lower 90s Saturday and Sunday.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
As of 130 AM Monday...

Nely flow around high pressure building across the Great Lakes and 
Middle Atlantic will become gusty into the teens kts with daytime 
heating primarily at FAY, and more briefly at RWI and RDU around 
midday. 

Outlook: High pressure over the Middle Atlantic will favor VFR 
conditions through mid week, with the exception of a chance of 
shallow, radiation fog/mist at RWI due to local effects. A frontal 
zone will settle into the NC with a chance of convection and 
associated flight restrictions on Fri. 

&&

.RAH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...MWS/Leins
AVIATION...MWS

briefing.headline: Quiet start, warmer later with rain risk Thu–Fri
briefing.summary: As of 5:02am Monday the NWS discussion says expect a dry, seasonable start to the week. Temperatures climb midweek with increasing chances for showers and storms late in the week.
briefing.nearTerm: Today will be mostly sunny with drier air keeping overnight lows and afternoon humidity lower than recently. East winds will be light and conditions should stay dry through Wednesday.
briefing.extended: A warming trend continues Wednesday into Thursday as southerly flow brings more humid air. A front moving in late Thursday into Friday will raise chances of showers and storms, then precipitation should ease behind the front for the weekend.
briefing.uncertainty: The main forecast uncertainty is the exact timing of the front and when shower and storm chances increase.

FXUS62 KMHX 070634
AFDMHX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Newport/Morehead City NC
234 AM EDT Mon Sep 7 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Return to more seasonable September temps for the beginning 
of the week with a warming trend developing late week ahead of 
the next front.

2) The next front will impact the area late week and this weekend,
with a return to unsettled weather. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...High pressure centered over the Great Lakes will
continue to build southeastward today, becoming centered over
the Mid-Atlantic and Carolinas Tuesday, before sliding offshore
Wed. This will keep a cooler/drier NE-E flow over the area, with
seasonable temps for early September and feeling much more 
comfortable, with highs in the 80s and dewpoints in the 60s/low 
70s. Temps will begin to warm mid to late week as southerly flow
re-develops ahead of the next front. Isolated coastal showers 
will be possible today, with bulk of activity remaining 
offshore. Mostly dry weather will then prevail through mid week
with drier air in place. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...The next front will approach the area late week,
possibly stalling over the area into the weekend. This will lead
to increasing precip chances Fri and Sat. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Pred VFR conditions expected through the period. NE-ENE wind
gusts 15-20 kt this afternoon. 

NOTE: AMD NOT SKED has been appended to the EWN TAFs as the 
site is not transmitting through normal channels. The site is 
still reporting via telephone so it will be monitored, but not 
as frequently as when it is completely operational. The next 
closest ASOS is at Cherry Point (KNKT).

Outlook (Tue through Fri): High pressure will build in from the
north through mid week, with pred VFR conditions expected.

&&

.MARINE...
Latest obs show NE-ENE winds 10-20 kt with seas 3-5 ft. High
pressure building in from the north will keep moderate to breezy
NE-ENE winds 15-25 kt across the area tonight, slowly easing 
through the day Tue. SCAs continue for the coastal waters and
Pamlico Sound into tonight and Tue. Seas will build to to 4-8 
ft today, highest across the outer waters, subsiding to 4-7 ft
Tue morning. 

Outlook (Tue through Fri): Winds and seas will begin to ease 
Tuesday and Wed as high pressure builds in. SW winds 5-15 kt 
return Wed night and Thu with seas 2-3 ft.

&&

.MHX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
NC...Beach Hazards Statement from 8 AM EDT this morning through 
     this evening for NCZ196-203>205.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory from 9 AM this morning to 8 PM EDT this 
     evening for AMZ135.
     Small Craft Advisory until midnight EDT tonight for AMZ150.
     Small Craft Advisory until noon EDT Tuesday for AMZ152-154.
     Small Craft Advisory until 2 PM EDT Tuesday for AMZ156-158.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...CQD/CEB
AVIATION...CQD/CEB
MARINE...CQD/CEB

briefing.headline: Seasonable start to week; front late week
briefing.summary: High pressure keeps the start of the week dry and more seasonable. A front late in the week may bring a return to unsettled weather.
briefing.nearTerm: Today will be mostly sunny with a northeast breeze and generally dry conditions. Coastal spots could see an isolated shower, but most rain should remain offshore.
briefing.extended: Temperatures will warm a bit mid to late week as southerly flow returns. Late week into the weekend the approaching front will raise the chance of showers and storms across the area.
briefing.uncertainty: Timing and stall location of the next front late week will change how widespread the rain will be.
